items.title: uv sync --inexact removes `.venv` and recreates it. It was not the case before.
items.reason: Closest prior report: it has the identical version-conflict diagnostic and recreation sequence. However, astral-sh/uv#16231 involved a copied environment with mismatched Python patch versions; it did not report that recreation retained the old interpreter.

items.title: failed to remove directory `/app/.venv`: Resource busy
items.reason: Related to the removal failure, but its fix addressed a busy mount-point directory, not permission denial while deleting `.venv/CACHEDIR.TAG`.

items.title: Reapply "Fix transparent Python upgrades in project environments"
items.reason: Establishes that environments backed by uv-managed minor-version links should survive patch upgrades. This report instead uses `/usr/local/bin/python3.12`, so that mechanism does not directly cover it.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests for the exact version-conflict, VIRTUAL_ENV, CACHEDIR.TAG, permission, and recreation diagnostics, plus conceptual terms involving pyvenv.cfg metadata, patch upgrades, system interpreters, copied or mounted environments, and active/project path mismatches. Fix-oriented searches covered transparent-upgrade and version_info changes. astral-sh/uv#19100 and astral-sh/uv#19102 concern exact patch pins following managed links; astral-sh/uv#19920, astral-sh/uv#19925, and astral-sh/uv#1689 concern pyvenv.cfg formatting; astral-sh/uv#7073 concerns an unnecessary warning under --no-sync.

type_reason: uv selects `/usr/local/bin/python3.12` as CPython 3.12.13 and recreates the environment from it, but `uv run python --version` still reports 3.12.2, leaving the mismatch in place for every subsequent run. No open issue or pull request tracks this same outcome, and the closest closed report had a materially different copied-environment setup.
summary: astral-sh/uv#16231 has the same mismatch diagnostic but a different copied-environment cause. astral-sh/uv#16218 covers a distinct mount removal failure, while astral-sh/uv#19928 applies only to uv-managed transparent upgrades. None tracks recreation continuing to execute the old Python patch.
draft_response:
The log confirms that uv recreates `.venv` because its interpreter reports Python 3.12.2 while the environment metadata records 3.12.13. What remains unexplained is why recreating it from `/usr/local/bin/python3.12`, which uv identifies as 3.12.13, still leaves `uv run python --version` reporting 3.12.2.

Could you share the output, immediately after recreation, of `/usr/local/bin/python3.12 -c 'import sys; print(sys.version); print(sys.executable); print(sys._base_executable)'`, the equivalent command using `.venv/bin/python`, `readlink -f .venv/bin/python`, and `cat .venv/pyvenv.cfg`? Please also say whether the repository or `.venv` is copied or mounted, and provide the owner and mode of `.venv` and `.venv/CACHEDIR.TAG`.

astral-sh/uv#16231 has the same conflict message, but involved copying an environment between container stages with different Python patch versions. This report also shows different active and project locations under `/mnt/hdd/Toolkits/Tools/AutotestServices` and `/mnt/hdd/Repositories/autotests_git`; the VIRTUAL_ENV warning is expected when those differ. Use `--active` only if the active environment is intentionally the target.
